title: Quant Tinker Notebook — quick eval notes & todo
content:
Daily tinker log (short, messy)

2026-03-18 morning: quick goals
- baseline latency for redwood-open-7b (fp16) on p4d: target p95 < 120ms for 64-token prompt.
- test GPTQ 4-bit (gptq-4bit-fast) vs bnb-int8 (bitsandbytes) on same host.
- run small eval set: 200 prompts (mix of instruction + long context).

Notes, commands tried
- eval command used (local):
  python bench_eval.py --model redwood-open-7b --device cuda:0 --batch 1 --seq 64 --quant gptq-4bit --group-size 128 --kv-cache true --out results/gptq-4b-run1.json
- quick bnb run: replace --quant bnb-int8 and add --bnb-block-size 32
- docker variant for dedicated node test: docker run --gpus all -v /mnt/models:/models bench:latest bash -lc "python bench_eval.py --model /models/redwood-open-7b --quant gptq-4bit --batch 2"

Results (raw, noisy) 2026-03-18
- fp16 baseline (p4d): median token time ~0.9ms, p95 request (64 tokens) ~110ms, mem 18.3GB
- gptq-4bit (group=128): median token time ~1.1ms, p95 130ms, mem 10.2GB -> good cost win but tail a bit worse
- bnb-int8 (block=32): median token time ~1.05ms, p95 125ms, mem 9.6GB -> similar to GPTQ but different tail patterns
- Observed token emission jitter when sequence crossed 512 boundary (weird spikes)

Quick analysis/notes
- latency tail seems correlated with KV-cache hits vs misses. When prompting with long prefixes (repeat context), we see p95 drop by ~15ms. Need a controlled test: constant prefix vs fresh prompt.
- hypothesis: GPTQ decoding kernel uses slightly different memory access pattern that stalls on certain attention alignment lengths. Add perf counters.
- memory measurements are host-reported; might be counting page faults. Re-run with nvidia-smi sampling at 100ms to confirm.

Prompt sets used (sample)
- instr_short_01: "Summarize: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. In one sentence."
- long_context_10: 3-paragraph context + question appended asking to extract timeline. (used to stress KV cache)
- code_completion_small: prompt with "# python function" and 12 tokens of signature

Evaluation notes
- quality delta between fp16 and gptq-4bit on instruction set (ROUGE-L proxy on 200 prompts): fp16 0.762, gptq-4bit 0.754 (small but visible regression on numeric answers)
- failure modes: hallucinated dates in timeline prompts for some quantized checkpoints (investigate tokenizer rounding?)

Open TODOs (priority order)
1) Re-run controlled kv-cache A/B: use same seed, two conditions: warm-cache vs cold-cache; record p50/p95/p99. Ticket: ENG-8876 (assigned to me).
2) Add perf hooks in bench harness to record GPU SM utilization and kernel durations (nvprof or CUPTI). Talk to Lin for CUPTI boilerplate.
3) Try GPTQ group-size 64 and 256 to see sensitivity. Log results in spreadsheet.
4) Small prompt set for function-calling style tests (edge-case deterministic failure). Create prompt templates and share with Nina.
5) If numeric regressions persist, try per-channel symmetric quant vs asymmetric (if supported by GPTQ build).

Mini plan for next session (2026-03-19)
- 09:00-10:30: controlled kv-cache experiments (cold/warm) on p4d-dedicated node; collect perf traces.
- 11:00: sync with Lin (15m) to instrument CUPTI.
- afternoon: run group-size sweep (64/128/256) for gptq and bnb-int8 block-size sweep (16/32/64).

Random scratch notes / things to remember
- Slack thread: #aml-kv-cache has a pointer to old PR where we saw p95 spikes (link pinned).
- PR referenced: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427 (look at kernel launch params)
- Confluence page: quant-playbook-v2 has recommended defaults but we may want different group-size for LLaMA-style weights.

Small reproducible snippet that failed once (keep here)
- reproducible seed case where model outputs truncated token mid-word:
  seed: 17342, prompt: instr_short_01, model: gptq-4bit-gs128, seq=512, batch=1
  observed: model stalls for ~2s at token 312 then emits remainder. Possibly kernel timeout or host sync.

Questions for Lin/Nina
- Lin: how to get wall-clock breakdown per kernel in Python harness without too much overhead?
- Nina: want to add a micro-eval for function-calling API with quantized models. Any test prompts we should include?

Notes-to-self (do not forget)
- tag results with bench config id (e.g., diego-20260318-gptq-gs128) and upload to S3 under s3://redwood-aml/benchmarks/diego/
- add small README to results folder explaining columns (latency, mem, kernel-hits)

End of log for now.

Streams / future ideas (brain dump)
- automated agent that picks group-size / block-size combinations and runs minimal eval to recommend Pareto frontier (latency vs mem vs quality). Could be a small Bayesian optimizer.
- explore hybrid quant (most sensitive layers in fp16, rest gptq) for better numeric fidelity.

-- Diego
